applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision over Matthew 1:16 by asking whether either text's own words state the contrary, which is the verse-level stating-verse inquiry Rule K-C governs and retires for chain-against-chain collisions.
quote: the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together: reading one applies the rule because the defender's cited texts must be weighed as a chain by footing; reading two treats the question text-by-text and asks whether any one text's own words state the contrary, which the rule forbids in this setting.
why: The judge uses the retired own-words contrary test to call Matthew 1:16 underdetermined instead of weighing the defender's cited texts as a chain by footing.
